# Packages


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
```
:::


## Working with multiple data frames

Often instead of being provided the data you need for your analysis in a single data frame, you will need to bring information from multiple datasets together into a data frame yourself. These datasets will be linked to each other via a column (usually an identifier, something that links the two datasets together) that you can use to join them together.

There are many possible types of joins. All have the format `something_join(x, y)`.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
x <- tibble(
  value = c(1, 2, 3),
  xcol = c("x1", "x2", "x3")
  )

y <- tibble(
  value = c(1, 2, 4),
  ycol = c("y1", "y2", "y4")
  )

x
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 3 × 2
  value xcol 
  <dbl> <chr>
1     1 x1   
2     2 x2   
3     3 x3   
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
y
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 3 × 2
  value ycol 
  <dbl> <chr>
1     1 y1   
2     2 y2   
3     4 y4   
```


:::
:::


We will demonstrate each of the joins on these small, toy datasets.

**Note: These functions below know to join `x` and `y` by `value` because each dataset has `value` as a column. See for yourself!**


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
names(x)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "value" "xcol" 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
names(y)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "value" "ycol" 
```


:::
:::


### `inner_join()`

only keeps observations from x that have a matching key in y.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
inner_join(x, y)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr}

```
Joining with `by = join_by(value)`
```


:::

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 2 × 3
  value xcol  ycol 
  <dbl> <chr> <chr>
1     1 x1    y1   
2     2 x2    y2   
```


:::
:::


### `left_join()`

A left_join() keeps all observations in x and includes what is matched with y


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
left_join(x , y, by = "value")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 3 × 3
  value xcol  ycol 
  <dbl> <chr> <chr>
1     1 x1    y1   
2     2 x2    y2   
3     3 x3    <NA> 
```


:::
:::


### `right_join()`

A right_join() keeps all observations in y and includes what is matched with x


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
right_join(x, y) 
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr}

```
Joining with `by = join_by(value)`
```


:::

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 3 × 3
  value xcol  ycol 
  <dbl> <chr> <chr>
1     1 x1    y1   
2     2 x2    y2   
3     4 <NA>  y4   
```


:::
:::


### `full_join()`

full_join() keeps all observations from x and y


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
full_join(x, y)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr}

```
Joining with `by = join_by(value)`
```


:::

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 4 × 3
  value xcol  ycol 
  <dbl> <chr> <chr>
1     1 x1    y1   
2     2 x2    y2   
3     3 x3    <NA> 
4     4 <NA>  y4   
```


:::
:::


### `semi_join()`

only shows x where key matches with x and y


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
semi_join(x, y)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr}

```
Joining with `by = join_by(value)`
```


:::

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 2 × 2
  value xcol 
  <dbl> <chr>
1     1 x1   
2     2 x2   
```


:::
:::


### `anti_join()`

shows the non-matching data found in x


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
anti_join(x, y)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr}

```
Joining with `by = join_by(value)`
```


:::

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 1 × 2
  value xcol 
  <dbl> <chr>
1     3 x3   
```


:::
:::


## Joining by more than one variable


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
x2 <- tibble(
  value = c(1, 2, 3),
  value2 = c(4,5,6),
  xcol = c("x1", "x2", "x3")
  )

y2<- tibble(
  value = c(1, 2, 4), 
  value2 = c(4,5,7),
  ycol = c("y1", "y2", "y4")
  )

x2
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 3 × 3
  value value2 xcol 
  <dbl>  <dbl> <chr>
1     1      4 x1   
2     2      5 x2   
3     3      6 x3   
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
y2
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 3 × 3
  value value2 ycol 
  <dbl>  <dbl> <chr>
1     1      4 y1   
2     2      5 y2   
3     4      7 y4   
```


:::
:::


### `inner_join()`


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
inner_join(x2, y2, by = c("value"))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 2 × 5
  value value2.x xcol  value2.y ycol 
  <dbl>    <dbl> <chr>    <dbl> <chr>
1     1        4 x1           4 y1   
2     2        5 x2           5 y2   
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
inner_join(x2, y2 , by = c("value" , "value2"))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 2 × 4
  value value2 xcol  ycol 
  <dbl>  <dbl> <chr> <chr>
1     1      4 x1    y1   
2     2      5 x2    y2   
```


:::
:::


### `left_join()`


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
left_join(x2 , y2, by = c("value"))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 3 × 5
  value value2.x xcol  value2.y ycol 
  <dbl>    <dbl> <chr>    <dbl> <chr>
1     1        4 x1           4 y1   
2     2        5 x2           5 y2   
3     3        6 x3          NA <NA> 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
left_join(x2 , y2, by = c("value" , "value2"))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 3 × 4
  value value2 xcol  ycol 
  <dbl>  <dbl> <chr> <chr>
1     1      4 x1    y1   
2     2      5 x2    y2   
3     3      6 x3    <NA> 
```


:::
:::
